accepted.s: Who identified the word ‘Nagabu’ in the Amaravati inscription?
accepted.x: Veturi Prabhakara Sastri identified ‘Nagabu’ as the first Telugu word in the Amaravati inscription.
accepted.tq: Test the scholar associated with a specific epigraphic identification.
accepted.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: ‘Vepuru’ appears in the Myakadoni inscription. ‘Andhrapatha’ belongs to the Mayidavolu plates, ‘Nagabu’ to Amaravati, and ‘-ambul’ to Vishnukundin plates.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure inscription–word pair and eliminate swapped locations.
accepted.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following words is NOT listed among the Telugu words occurring in Hala’s Gatha Saptasati?
accepted.x: The listed words include atta, addam, potta, tuppu, padi, pandi and pilla. Vepuru belongs to the Myakadoni inscription.
accepted.tq: Find the odd item by separating literary evidence from inscriptional evidence.
accepted.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Telugu plural suffix ‘-ambul’ is found in the:
accepted.x: The Vishnukundin Chikkulla plates use the Telugu plural suffix ‘-ambul’, as in ‘Vijayarajya Samvatsarambul’.
accepted.tq: Test the exact grammatical form against its inscriptional source.
accepted.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: ‘Andhrapatha’ was first recorded in the:
accepted.x: ‘Andhrapatha’ is first recorded in the Mayidavolu plates of Pallava Sivaskandavarman, written in Prakrit around 300 CE.
accepted.tq: Link the distinctive term with its earliest recorded source.
accepted.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the development of Telugu script:
1. Brahmi is the source of the Telugu script.
2. Satavahana inscriptions were written in Prakrit using Brahmi script.
3. Telugu and Kannada began to differentiate during the Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya age.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu script developed from Brahmi; Satavahana inscriptions used Prakrit and Brahmi; and differentiation from Kannada began during the Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya age.
accepted.tq: Combine source, language and script-development statements before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Bhattiprolu stupa inscriptions are best described as:
o: Sanskrit inscriptions in the common Old Kannada script
Tamil inscriptions in the Grantha script
Prakrit inscriptions in a variant of Brahmi carrying early Telugu place and personal names
Telugu inscriptions in the fully developed medieval Telugu script
accepted.x: The Bhattiprolu inscriptions, dated approximately to 400 BCE in Guntur, use a variant of Brahmi and contain early Telugu place and personal names.
accepted.tq: Use the precise combination of date, place, script and linguistic evidence.
accepted.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages in the evolution of Telugu script in chronological order:
A. Separate Telugu script with rounded letters and vowel signs
B. Bhattiprolu variant of Brahmi
C. Common Old Kannada–Telugu script
D. Beginning of differentiation between Telugu and Kannada
accepted.x: The sequence is Bhattiprolu Brahmi variant, common Old Kannada–Telugu script, differentiation during the Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya age, and separate Telugu script in the 11th–14th centuries.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest script stage first and then place the transition stages.
accepted.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly reflects the chronology of the emergence of the distinct Telugu script?
o: It emerged only after the 14th century.
It developed directly from the Tamil script during the 4th century BCE.
It was fully distinct during the Satavahana period.
It had emerged by the 11th century, with full separation placed broadly in the 11th–14th centuries.
accepted.x: One account places the emergence of distinct Telugu script by the 11th century, while another describes full separation over the 11th–14th centuries.
accepted.tq: Reconcile close chronological formulations instead of treating them as contradictory.
accepted.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Telugu belongs to which sub-branch of the Dravidian language family?
accepted.x: Telugu belongs to the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
accepted.tq: Test the exact linguistic sub-classification rather than the broader family name.
accepted.sec: Dravidian family - sub-branch, sister languages  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following are identified as sister languages of Telugu within the South-Central Dravidian group?
accepted.x: Gondi and Kui are identified among the sister languages of Telugu in the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
accepted.tq: Distinguish sister languages from other Dravidian languages outside the stated sub-branch.
accepted.sec: Dravidian family - sub-branch, sister languages  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Telugu:
1. It is the official language of Andhra Pradesh.
2. It is included among the 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule.
3. It belongs to the Indo-Aryan language family.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh and one of the 22 Eighth Schedule languages. It belongs to the Dravidian, not Indo-Aryan, family.
accepted.tq: Reject the broad-family trap while retaining the constitutional and state-language facts.
accepted.sec: Dravidian family - sub-branch, sister languages  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The theory that Telugu grew out of the Desi bhasha, identified with Paisachi of Prakrit, is associated with the view that:
o: Telugu was created by the Kakatiya court
Desi words show close resemblance to Telugu
accepted.x: The stated theory connects Telugu with the Desi bhasha or Paisachi of Prakrit, and D.C. Sircar observed that Desi words were very close to Telugu.
accepted.tq: Connect the etymological theory with the linguistic evidence cited for it.
accepted.sec: Dravidian family - sub-branch, sister languages  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Trilinga theory derives the name Andhra from the three Shaiva centres of:
accepted.x: The Trilinga theory refers to Srisailam, Kaleshwaram and Draksharama as the three Shaiva centres of Trilinga desa.
accepted.tq: Use a three-place association to distinguish the Trilinga theory from other regional lists.
accepted.sec: Names of the language - etymology theories  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Telugu — derived by all scholars exclusively from Tamil
Trilinga — associated with three Shaiva centres
Andhrika — an alternative name of the language
Tenugu — derived by some from tene, meaning honey
accepted.x: The material presents Telugu, Andhra, Andhrika and Tenugu as names or theories of origin; it does not support an exclusive Tamil derivation accepted by all scholars.
accepted.tq: Identify the overgeneralised attribution using the extreme word ‘all’.
accepted.sec: Names of the language - etymology theories  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Telugu was declared a Classical Language by the Government of India in:
accepted.x: Telugu was granted Classical Language status by the Union Government in 2008, together with Kannada.
accepted.tq: Use the year options to distinguish Telugu’s status from Tamil’s earlier recognition.
accepted.sec: Classical language status - year, criteria  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the recognition of Classical Languages is correct?
o: The Government of Uttar Pradesh granted Classical Language status to Telugu.
Tamil was recognised in 2008, after Telugu.
Telugu and Kannada were recognised in 2008, while Tamil was the first in 2004.
Malayalam and Odia were recognised in 2008 along with Telugu.
accepted.x: Tamil was the first, receiving recognition in 2004. Telugu and Kannada received it in 2008; the granting authority was the Union Government, not Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Trap the swapped year and wrong authority in a recognition-related statement.
accepted.sec: Classical language status - year, criteria  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the years in which Malayalam and Odia received Classical Language status?
accepted.x: Malayalam received Classical Language status in 2013 and Odia in 2014.
accepted.tq: Separate nearby recognition years instead of grouping all languages under 2008.
accepted.sec: Classical language status - year, criteria  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (Author)
a. Vidyanatha
b. Jayapa Senani
c. Sakalya Mallabhattu
List-II (Association)
i. Named among Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court
ii. Prataparudra Yashobhushanam
iii. Nritta Ratnavali, Geeta Ratnavali and Vadya Ratnavali
accepted.x: Vidyanatha wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam; Jayapa Senani wrote the three Ratnavali works; Sakalya Mallabhattu is named among the Sanskrit authors.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive group of three works associated with Jayapa Senani.
accepted.sec: Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Jayapa Senani held the office of Gajasahini under Ganapatideva. The office refers to his role as:
accepted.x: Gajasahini means commander of the elephant corps. Jayapa Senani’s military office should not be confused with the subjects of his Ratnavali works.
accepted.tq: Use the occupational meaning of the title to avoid the profession trap.
accepted.sec: Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which attribution is specifically identified as requiring caution because of differing evidence?
accepted.x: Ravipati Tripurantakudu is credited with the Sanskrit Niroshthya Ramayanam, but an APP fragment attributes Niroshtya Ramayana and Udara Raghavam to Takavelli Mallikarju Bhattu.
accepted.tq: Recognise the source-attribution dispute rather than treating similar author claims as identical.
accepted.sec: Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Tikkana’s title ‘Ubhayakavimitrudu’ is associated with his position as a poet in the court of:
accepted.x: Tikkana was associated with the court of Manumasiddhi II of Nellore and bore the title Ubhayakavimitrudu.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Tikkana’s patron from the Kakatiya rulers connected with his period.
accepted.sec: Tikkana - patron, parvas, independent works, philosophy  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an independent work of Tikkana rather than a portion of his Mahabharata translation?
accepted.x: Krishna Satakam is listed as an independent work of Tikkana. The other works are associated with different authors or literary contexts.
accepted.tq: Separate a poet’s independent work from works of nearby authors and traditions.
accepted.sec: Tikkana - patron, parvas, independent works, philosophy  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Tikkana’s Harihara philosophy was intended principally to:
o: Separate religious literature from royal patronage
Replace Telugu with Sanskrit in court literature
accepted.x: Tikkana propounded Harihara philosophy, described as Harihara Dvaitam, to reconcile Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions.
accepted.tq: Infer the practical religious purpose from the philosophical label.
accepted.sec: Tikkana - patron, parvas, independent works, philosophy  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (Siva Kavi)
a. Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya
b. Nannechoda
c. Palkuriki Somanatha
List-II (Work or contribution)
i. Basava Puranam and Panditaradhya Charitra
ii. Sivatattvasaram
iii. Kumarasambhavam
accepted.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya is associated with Sivatattvasaram, Nannechoda with Kumarasambhavam, and Palkuriki Somanatha with Basava Puranam and Panditaradhya Charitra.
accepted.tq: Match the poets through their distinctive Shaiva works.
accepted.sec: Siva Kavis (Shaiva Kavitrayam) → works  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the claims regarding the first Satakam?
o: Sivatattvasaram is identified in one source, while Vrushadhipa Satakam is identified in another.
Only Vrushadhipa Satakam is ever identified as the first Satakam.
Basava Puranam is identified by both sources as the first Satakam.
Only Sivatattvasaram is ever identified as the first Satakam.
accepted.x: The sources differ: one identifies Sivatattvasaram as the first Satakam, while another identifies Vrushadhipa Satakam.
accepted.tq: Handle a documented source variation without converting it into a false single-answer claim.
accepted.sec: Siva Kavis (Shaiva Kavitrayam) → works  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Nannechoda is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Vrushadhipa Satakam and the title Gajasahini
Basava Puranam and the title Prabandha Parameswara
accepted.x: Nannechoda wrote Kumarasambhavam and bore the title Kavirajasekhara. He is also associated with eight descriptions characteristic of the prabandha tradition.
accepted.tq: Combine the work and title that belong to the same poet.
accepted.sec: Siva Kavis (Shaiva Kavitrayam) → works  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Kreedabhiramam is credited to Vinukonda Vallabharaya, also known as:
accepted.x: Kreedabhiramam is credited to Vinukonda Vallabharaya, who was also known as Vallabhamatya.
accepted.tq: Test the alternate name of the attributed author.
accepted.sec: Kreedabhiramam - authorship and city  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The authorship debate concerning Kreedabhiramam arises partly because it is a Telugu rendering of which Sanskrit play?
accepted.x: Kreedabhiramam is regarded as a Telugu rendering of Ravipati Tripurantakudu’s Sanskrit play Premabhiramam, creating an attribution issue alongside its credit to Vallabharaya.
accepted.tq: Separate the Telugu rendering, its Sanskrit source and the credited author.
accepted.sec: Kreedabhiramam - authorship and city  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following features is associated with the Orugallu described in Kreedabhiramam?
o: The maritime trade of Motupalli alone
Markets, nightlife and the Kakati Devi temple
Only the military fortifications of the city
accepted.x: Kreedabhiramam describes Orugallu, or Warangal, through its markets, nightlife and Kakati Devi temple, and calls it ‘Andhra Nagari’.
accepted.tq: Select the cluster of urban features actually described in the work.
accepted.sec: Kreedabhiramam - authorship and city  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Kreedabhiramam belongs to the post-Kakatiya period associated with the:
accepted.x: Kreedabhiramam was written in the post-Kakatiya period associated with the Reddi era.
accepted.tq: Use the dynastic-period clue rather than the city’s earlier Kakatiya association.
accepted.sec: Kreedabhiramam - authorship and city  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Vrushadhipa Satakam is attributed to Palkuriki Somanatha. Sumati Satakam was composed by Baddena, while Sivatattvasaram belongs to Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya.
accepted.tq: Use author–Satakam pairings to distinguish closely related early Telugu works.
accepted.sec: Early Satakas → author  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Baddena, the author of Sumati Satakam, is also associated with the title or work:
accepted.x: Baddena is associated with Sumati Satakam and Nitisastra Muktavali.
accepted.tq: Link the author with the second work listed alongside the better-known Satakam.
accepted.sec: Early Satakas → author  [GROUP-II]
